newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-F.A. CUP SEMIFINALISTS FAIL TO SHINE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-F.A. CUP SEMIFINALISTS FAIL TO SHINE.

text.p: Chelsea, Wimbledon and Middlesbrough all failed to boost their supporters' confidence ahead of Sunday's F.A. Cup semifinals with disappointing English league results on Wednesday.
Chelsea suffered the worst blow to morale with a 3-1 defeat at Coventry, conceding three second-half goals in nine minutes against a side still deeply involved in the relegation battle.
Their semifinal opponents Wimbledon slumped to a 2-0 home defeat by Aston Villa, while Middlesborough also had a blank night in a goalless draw at fellow strugglers West Ham.

Ruud Gullit's Chelsea side could at least claim they were suffering something of an identity crisis, being forced to play in Coventry's away shirts when the referee decided there was a colour clash before kick-off.

But after Paul Hughes had scored in the 43rd minute to give them a halftime lead, Dion Dublin and Paul Williams netted twice in two minutes to put Coventry in front and Noel Whelan capitalised on an error by Norwegian goalkeeper Forde Grodas to make it three after 58 minutes.
The result lifted Coventry, who beat Liverpool on Sunday, to sixth from bottom but the relegation picture remains far from clear.
A 90th-minute own goal from Derby's Darryl Powell was enough to earn Southampton a 1-1 draw and lifted them off the bottom on goal difference above Nottingham Forest.
But five clubs are now separated by just three points with three automatic relegation places to be filled and Middlesbrough remain deep in trouble despite their excellent Cup form.
Everton did their best to scramble clear with a 1-1 home draw against Leicester and competition for European qualification is becoming equally fierce.

Sheffield Wednesday moved above Chelsea into sixth place with a 2-1 home win over Tottenham, while Savo Milosevic and Alan Wright took Villa into fourth place with the goals against a savagely weakened Wimbledon side.
First division Bolton made sure of the first division title with a 2-1 win at Manchester City.
